scope.databases: Dedicated browser-validation copies only; no original service/database touched.

outcome: Integrated old-layout comparison and new-home room/photo journeys passed at both viewports. Original workshop comparison passed after using its actual menu entry; original harness failures remain recorded.

visualReview.finding: The same legacy saved structure and planet objects remain unchanged before/after UI inspection; the comparison fixture contains a single floor blueprint and two lamps, so it is not evidence of complex-building editing.

New exterior and independent room share cream plaster, warm boards, muted green furniture/door, low specular response and restrained dark outlines. Door opening remains readable beside the unchanged character.

Ground close camera is closer than the original baseline: character is more legible, while the nearby parked ship can leave the frame. This is composition change, not unchanged-camera material A/B evidence.

World overview preserves the terrain biome colour and rock patches. Generated normal path pieces are visible with intended grass gaps; no route-surface fragments were observed in these captured views. This does not prove all route angles or seeds.
390px room follow intentionally crops lateral room edges. Whole-room and photo framing show the complete room; interactive controls remain visible.

2K local-geometry PNG exports have clean scene-only output, full room framing, and no UI. Portrait output uses large top/bottom space to fit the full width; zoom/orbit remain user controls. Both photo closes returned to the room UI.
All observed pages and shader compilation paths had zero pageerror and console.error events. No art code repair or rebuild was needed after this visual review.

limitations: Chrome 154.0.8037.98 on Apple M3/16GiB, ANGLE Metal; 390px is desktop touch emulation, not a physical phone.
Static counters and short rAF samples are diagnostic only. Other validation overlapped part of the time; no sustained/mobile/GPU performance conclusion is drawn.
This art pass did not exercise flight to the public hub or the full quest; the separate journey validation owns that scope.
Visual finishing is cosmetic and deterministic. It never invents structural roof/support members, closes openings, changes collision or modifies saved blueprint documents.

The first baseline attempt assumed the newer edit-structure button. A second temporary script lookup also used the wrong nested blueprint ID. Neither was a product error; corrected menu/library runs passed at both viewports.
